title: Flooring Adhesives and Flammable Liquids
summary: Many flooring adhesives, primers and cleaning solvents are flammable liquids. This talk covers OSHA's rules for containers, storage and keeping ignition sources away.
talking_points: Only approved containers and portable tanks may be used for storing and handling flammable liquids. Approved safety cans or DOT-approved containers are required for quantities of 5 gallons or less (with an exception for highly viscid materials), and original containers may be used for one gallon or less (29 CFR 1926.152(a)(1)).
Flammable liquids must not be stored in exits, stairways or places normally used for safe passage (1926.152(a)(2)).
No more than 25 gallons of flammable liquids may be stored in a room outside of an approved storage cabinet (1926.152(b)(1)).
Keep Category 1, 2 and 3 flammable liquids in closed containers when not actually in use (1926.152(f)(1)).
Dispose of leaks and spills promptly and safely (1926.152(f)(2)).

Category 1, 2 or 3 flammable liquids may be used only where there are no open flames or other ignition sources within 50 feet of the operation, unless conditions warrant more clearance (1926.152(f)(3)).
Smoking must be prohibited near operations that create a fire hazard, and the area must be posted "No Smoking or Open Flame" (1926.151(a)(3)).
Check the label and the safety data sheet to find out whether the product is flammable and what category it falls in.
site_hazards_to_check: Open adhesive pails or solvent cans
Pilot lights, heaters or sparks within 50 feet of the work
Spills on the subfloor or rags soaked with solvent
Flammables stored in stairways or exits
More than 25 gallons stored outside a cabinet
discussion_questions: Where do we store adhesives and solvents on this job?
What ignition sources are within 50 feet of where we will work?
Who has read the SDS for the product we use today?
